contract objectives as well. The overall rating for this factor is Excellent."</p><p class="body source">CMS Design Challenge Selection Committee</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) help millions of people every year find and enroll in health care programs. Planning a large-scale web and content management project to improve the customer experience of their multiple websites, the agency launched a design challenge for the vendors that were finalists for the contract.</p>
<p>We did a fast-paced collaboration with our partners <a href="https://fearless.tech/">Fearless</a> and <a href="https://www.kpmg.us/">KPMG</a> to submit deliverables in just 8 business days (including page designs, content recommendations, an API, and a clickable prototype with a smart chatbot). Our team won the challenge because the agency saw we could help them achieve their goal to better serve Medicare beneficiaries.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>The task was to redesign the <a href="https://www.medicare.gov/drug-coverage-part-d">Medicare Part D</a> section of the medicare.gov website, which helps people understand insurance options for their medication needs. For all their digital platforms, CMS needs to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Meet public expectation for easily navigable online services</li>
<li>Securely manage personal info and transactions for millions of beneficiaries</li>
<li>Provide friendly online experience for people facing stressful health situations</li>
<li>Serve diverse groups of users with competing wants and priorities</li>
<li>Support agency staff in publishing clear and accurate public-facing content</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Agile Methodologies</li>
<li>User Research</li>
<li>Heuristic Evaluation</li>
<li>Persona & Scenario Design</li>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Content Strategy</li>
<li>Workflow & Interaction Design</li>
<li>Prototype Development & Testing</li>
<li>Visual Design</li>
<li>Mobile Optimization</li>
<li>API Design & Deployment</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Proto.io</li>
<li>Sketch</li>
<li>Invision</li>
<li>Mural</li>
<li>Chatbot AI</li>
<li>Gitlab</li>
<li>Drupal</li>
<li>Pa11y</li>
<li>Solr</li>
<li>AWS Kubernetes</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>Within the time constraint for this compressed agile design sprint, we conducted lean versions of the activities we would normally do to make sure the site was effective for Medicare recipients. Daily collaboration among all team members, from Design to DevOps to Developers, allowed us to quickly test and iterate on every step.</p>
<p>We used <a href="https://www.drupal.org/industries/government">Drupal</a> as our preferred open source platform and the <a href="https://design.cms.gov/">CMS design system</a>, which builds on the U.S. Web Design System. Together, these tools provide a solid foundation for <a href="https://medium.com/civicactions/4-ways-to-improve-government-accessibility-through-open-source-8e20fabc7281">accessible government websites</a> — a key goal for agencies like CMS that serve diverse and aging populations.</p>
<p>Human Centered Design played a critical role in our process of building a site that would be intuitive and useful to older Americans seeking information about their drug coverage options.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Understand the needs</h3><div class="body"><p>We talked to real Medicare beneficiaries to understand the challenges they faced in navigating the site. Based on what they said, we created a <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/19f_pUBSrIRxDJdnvNa4uROiP_QwQKWoh/view?usp=sharing">key persona</a> to drive our scenario-based approach —  ensuring that our work solved real problems and created value for users. We also evaluated the existing site to see how well it met <a href="https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/">standards for usability</a>.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/WECMS_Design_1_9ecc4b385b/WECMS_Design_1_9ecc4b385b.jpg" alt="Graphic of a "key persona" that we made to help us understand the needs of real Medicare beneficiaries."><div class="caption">Our key persona "Sam" reflected what real Medicare users think and feel as they use the site.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Offer customized guidance</h3><div class="body"><p>To help visitors feel comfortable navigating complex information about benefits coverage, we created several experience options for them to choose from. They could explore the site on their own, use the guidance wizard, or ask questions of the interactive chat bot. We also improved the Search function to deliver more relevant results.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/WECMS_Design_2_14bc59a349/WECMS_Design_2_14bc59a349.jpg" alt="Sticky notes showing the needs of users, to help us prioritize the work."><div class="caption">User research revealed what was working well and what could be improved.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Clear the path to success</h3><div class="body"><p>We focused on removing obstacles to help more people successfully find the information they needed. This was done through intuitive navigation and labels, scannable and actionable content, and a refreshed, accessible design. We tested our solutions with users and iterated based on their feedback.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/WECMS_Design_3_9d775961d5/WECMS_Design_3_9d775961d5.jpg" alt="Diagram showing how Medicare beneficiaries get to the various services they need."><div class="caption">We focused on removing obstacles so beneficiaries could easily find important and relevant information.</div></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Research-based solution</p><div class="body"><p>Because we spoke to Medicare recipients and validated our proposed solutions with them, CMS knows that real user needs will be met with the redesigned site, helping people access benefits more easily.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Consistent online experience</p><div class="body"><p>Medicare.gov visitors deserve a consistent experience across all parts of the site, on any device. Our design uses a mobile-first approach and a color palette that provides smooth transitions between pages.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Accessible healthcare services</p><div class="body"><p>The prototype is compliant with <a href="https://www.section508.gov/blog/accessibility-news-the-section-508-Update">Section 508</a>, using intuitive design and clear language to make complex medical insurance information easily accessible by the broadest possible representation of the public.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Data to help others</p><div class="body"><p>Doctors, app developers, health information curators, and others can pull valuable Medicare data for their own use through the API integration we created using the JSON:API that is part of Drupal core.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Simplified content management</p><div class="body"><p>The prototype showed how CMS staff can more easily get the right information to the right people using templates and workflows in Drupal, customized for the agency’s various departments and content needs.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Efficient and reliable technology</p><div class="body"><p>We built the prototype using the same Agile and DevOps practices that we would on a larger scale — with streamlined workflows that allow us to build, test, and deploy new code quickly and securely.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Let’s build a public success story.</h2><span class="h3">Get in touch to start.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button class="inner"><h1>Modernizing and Streamlining Cybersecurity Information</h1><span class="client-name">Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services</span><p class="body">We worked alongside ISPG customers and stakeholders to design and build a searchable, user-friendly portal for cybersecurity information – making it easier for security personnel to keep CMS data and systems safe. </p></div></section><section class="case-study--hero-image"><div class="inner"><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/cybergeek_hero_2b25a8ab03/cybergeek_hero_2b25a8ab03.png" alt="A webpage with a welcome message for the CMS Information Security and Privacy Group (ISPG). It describes ISPG's role within CMS's Office of Information Technology, focusing on security and privacy."><span class="caption">The new ISPG website at security.cms.gov is a customer-centric portal for security information at CMS.</span></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">95% </h2><p class="body stat--text">of ISPG’s static PDF documents converted to accessible HTML content</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">240+ </h2><p class="body stat--text">CMS systems protected by ISPG’s security policies & programs</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">1 </h2><p class="body stat--text">trusted source for CMS security and privacy information</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“This is the best effort to date to get all of the security and privacy information in one place, in a way that makes sense. This is modern government information delivery at its best.”
</p><p class="body source">CMS Program Leader</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The CMS Information Security and Privacy Group (ISPG) is in charge of the policies and programs that ensure the security and privacy of data that is handled by CMS information systems. ISPG staff and contractors work to maintain policies, distribute guidance, communicate with customers, support security programs, and promote new initiatives.</p>
<p>While doing this important work over the years, they amassed a large collection of documents and resources that were spread across various locations and formats. This led to issues with version control and made it hard for people to find the information needed to do their security-related tasks.</p>
<p>Without a single, trusted location for cybersecurity information – and with many of the documents being in static PDFs that were full of jargon and hard to understand – finding  essential information from ISPG could be onerous, negatively impacting CMS’ overall security posture.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>To improve their customer service and promote better security across CMS systems, ISPG engaged our team to develop a user-friendly website (informally known as “CyberGeek”) at security.cms.gov that is recognized as the authoritative home for CMS security and privacy information. With this project, ISPG aims to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Improve customer service through modern information delivery</li>
<li>Support CMS security personnel with the resources needed for their critical work</li>
<li>Make security topics and policies more approachable and human-centered</li>
<li>Build user-friendly processes to help ISPG staff maintain their content</li>
<li>Establish a platform where customers can find news and updates from ISPG</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Product Strategy</li>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Communications Strategy</li>
<li>Content Design</li>
<li>Plain Language Writing</li>
<li>User Research & Testing</li>
<li>Prototype Development & Testing</li>
<li>UX / UI Design</li>
<li>Stakeholder Engagement</li>
<li>Frontend Development</li>
<li>Decoupled Methodology</li>
<li>Continuous Integration & Deployment</li>
<li>Drupal Customization</li>
<li>Accessibility Testing</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Figma</li>
<li>Mural</li>
<li>Storybook</li>
<li>Airtable</li>
<li>batCAVE (Platform-As-A-Service provided by CMS)</li>
<li>Drupal 10</li>
<li>React JS</li>
<li>Algolia Search</li>
<li>Google Analytics</li>
<li>Google Search Console</li>
<li>Axe</li>
<li>Pa11y</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our Approach</h2><div class="body"><p>Together with our partner <a href="https://affixdigital.io/">Affix Digital</a>, we worked closely with ISPG stakeholders and customers to understand the cybersecurity ecosystem at CMS. We built relationships across ISPG and partnered with their leadership and program teams to streamline their content into a single, trusted platform that makes cybersecurity information approachable and human-centered.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>First, listen and learn</h3><div class="body"><p>We started by interviewing ISPG customers to make sure we built the site’s information architecture in a way that made sense to the people using it. Card sorting – a process that involves users in the design of the site navigation – helped solidify the menus and categories that would be the foundation of a user’s journey through the site.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/cybergeek_1_c0b6688a32/cybergeek_1_c0b6688a32.png" alt="A dashboard screenshot showing various categories like CMS, Risk Management, Privacy Policy, and more. Each category contains different selections with some having lists of items and others with icons."><div class="caption"> We involved ISPG customers and program leaders at every step of our design process, and tested our assumptions with User Experience (UX) best practices.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Open source and accessible</h3><div class="body"><p>We built a decoupled site using <a href="https://www.drupal.org/industries/government">Drupal</a> and <a href="https://react.dev/">React</a> to give the client flexibility for technology changes in the future. Utilizing the <a href="https://designsystem.digital.gov/">U.S. Web Design System </a>(USWDS), we created a component library that ensures the site meets government requirements for things like accessibility and mobile responsiveness. We used <a href="https://storybook.js.org/">Storybook</a> to build components in isolation before deployment to the site, catching errors in real-time so they could be fixed on the spot.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Search at the core</h3><div class="body"><p>One of the main problems ISPG wanted to solve for their customers was the headache of searching for security documents, templates, and program information – which had been difficult to find in various internal repositories. We implemented a powerful search feature using Algolia, with filter options to help people find information specific to their needs. Improvements to search are ongoing as we learn more about how people use it.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/cybergeek_2_4122bb5f5d/cybergeek_2_4122bb5f5d.png" alt="Risk management and resources page: A webpage with tools and information to help manage and mitigate risks effectively."><div class="caption">ISPG customers report that the new CyberGeek search is a huge improvement on the prior experience.</div></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Improved customer experience</p><div class="body"><p>From Information System Security Officers (ISSOs) to Business and System Owners, the new website provides a better experience for people who need to interact with ISPG as part of the security compliance process at CMS.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Searchable and intuitive site</p><div class="body"><p>User and stakeholder interviews revealed that ISPG customers are loving the website’s powerful search feature, intuitive navigation, and clean design. Cybersecurity staff can focus on their work without wasting time hunting for information.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Accessible & approachable policy guidance</p><div class="body"><p>Complex security policies and processes are easier to understand now that ISPG’s guidance documents are written in plain language, with user needs and accessibility best practices at the forefront.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Simple content management </p><div class="body"><p>ISPG staff can access the pages they are responsible for managing through a user-friendly content management interface in Drupal. The workflows are designed to support busy staff and reduce content publishing bottlenecks.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Trusted communication channel</p><div class="body"><p>ISPG staff had struggled to communicate critical program updates effectively across many different platforms. The blog on their new website streamlines messaging into one trusted channel.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Ongoing partnership</p><div class="body"><p>To ensure the ongoing success of the ISPG website, we engaged deeply with ISPG teams all along the way, helping them evolve their organizational processes and sharing best practices for modern web content management.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--staff"><div class="inner"><h2>Meet the team</h2><div class="related-staff--wrapper"><div class="related-staff"><div class="inner"><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/LINCS_hero_a62d9ee986/LINCS_hero_a62d9ee986.png" alt="Modernized LINCS homepage displayed on laptop and mobile"><span class="caption">Educators and learners have a better user experience on the modernized LINCS websites, so they can find needed resources faster.</span></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">31,000 +</h2><p class="body stat--text">practitioners using these sites for professional development</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">30,000 +</h2><p class="body stat--text">helpdesk tickets resolved to improve user experience</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">76</h2><p class="body stat--text">commits made to the Drupal community on behalf of the agency</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“I’m truly impressed with [CivicActions'] customer care and the emotional intelligence evident in your approach to helpdesk support. Thank you!”</p><p class="body source">Education practitioner in the LINCS community</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>When we first engaged with the Department of Education, they needed help consolidating and updating their collection of websites for the Literacy and Information Communication System (LINCS), which supports adult education practitioners in their goal of helping adult learners transition to post-secondary education and 21st-century jobs.</p>
<p>LINCS offers support to individual practitioners as well as U.S. community, state, and Federal programs that promote literacy, making it a  unique resource for both individual educators and government-funded programs alike.</p>
<p>LINCS gives educators and learners access to resource libraries, discussion groups, and self-guided courses — but these were located on various websites that were outdated and confusing to navigate. LINCS needed to be restructured with modern, secure technical architecture. LINCS users also needed reliable, friendly support to resolve technical and login issues and get back to helping adult learners.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>To provide a valuable and secure learning platform for thousands of education practitioners, the Department of Education needed to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Update and consolidate numerous LINCS  websites and resources</li>
<li>Provide prompt helpdesk support for the large user community</li>
<li>Improve site navigation with user-centered design</li>
<li>Maintain a secure and reliable platform</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Learning Management Systems</li>
<li>Open-Source Software</li>
<li>Systems Administration</li>
<li>Cybersecurity Requirements Compliance</li>
<li>UX User Support, Research, & Design</li>
<li>Customer Support</li>
<li>Federal IT Requirements Compliance</li>
<li>Online Communities of Practice</li>
<li>Usability & Design</li>
<li>Cloud Migration & Hosting</li>
<li>Continuous Improvement</li>
<li>Infrastructure as Code: Kubernetes & Terraform, Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment pipelines</li>
<li>DevOps</li>
<li>Project Management</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Drupal 10</li>
<li>Moodle</li>
<li>Cypress</li>
<li>Axe accessibility testing</li>
<li>Lando</li>
<li>Docker</li>
<li>GitLab CI</li>
<li>Kubernetes</li>
<li>Flux</li>
<li>Terraform</li>
<li>AWS</li>
<li>SAML</li>
<li>Jira</li>
<li>GitLab</li>
<li>U.S. Web Design System</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>Our engagement with LINCS began as we transitioned the service’s website hosting to secure Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud servers, then used a modern <a href="https://www.drupal.org/industries/government">Drupal</a> content management system to consolidate the overabundance of outdated websites that LINCS had inherited from other departments. We used the <a href="https://designsystem.digital.gov/">U.S. Web Design System</a> to make the updated websites easy to navigate and mobile friendly.</p>
<p>Our partnership with LINCS is ongoing — we now provide continuous improvements to their platforms using Information Technology Agile Development methods. We work closely with program managers to help them get the most business value from their IT applications. This includes the maintenance and enhancement of LINCS websites, web-based tools, databases, search engines, streaming media, content management, and learning management systems.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Provide a seamless experience</h3><div class="body"><p>The main <a href="https://lincs.ed.gov/">LINCS website</a> serves as a central hub and brand for the Division of Adult Education and Literacy’s (DAEL) national leadership investments. To create a unified look-and-feel among the disparate supplementary LINCS websites, we did a visual redesign based on user research — creating a seamless experience for practitioners to access the resources they need.</p>
<p>Of late, our redesign has extended to information architecture, rendering global navigation more intuitive and informative, and revamping the way that site resources are organized and searched for.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/LINCS_1_09a3754dbf/LINCS_1_09a3754dbf.png" alt="Education practitioner using the LINCS community portal on a laptop"><div class="caption">Educators can access resources and discussion groups through the LINCS online community.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Use helpdesk feedback for iterative improvement</h3><div class="body"><p>Our support team provides fast, friendly resolution of technical and login issues for LINCS users, so they can get back to work quickly. Since our improvement of LINCS products is user-focused, we tie the helpdesk into the agile development process through daily communication between support staff and development teams. This ensures that system improvements are prioritized based on real user needs.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Increase efficiencies for cost savings</h3><div class="body"><p>We implement automation and efficiency for the LINCS systems wherever possible. This helps prevent the buildup of technical debt and gives the Department of Education the most value for its investment in LINCS. We improve operations through DevOps practices including system administration, continuous integration, code standardization, lifecycle development, and quality control.</p>
<p>A recent highlight of this approach is our campaign toward Infrastructure as Code, or IaC, which automates the management and monitoring of our site architecture. IaC dramatically enhances the security, stability, and scalability of all LINCS sites, and increases both the efficiency and consistency of our development workflows. Following the IaC production deployment, we’ll be able to further consolidate our server and storage architecture, substantially reducing both their complexity and their cost. And following this, the next major phase of this initiative is the use of our automated tools and processes to process and monitor our Compliance documentation, boosting efficiency and scalability in this arena as well.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Empowered educators</p><div class="body"><p>The core LINCS community is a passionate group of educators committed to making a difference for adult learners. These web platforms help them access high-quality information and free professional development opportunities.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">User-centered improvements</p><div class="body"><p>LINCS is constantly improved through user feedback via our helpdesk support services. The agency can rest assured that they are prioritizing the right things through an agile and user-informed process.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Secure web platforms</p><div class="body"><p>By migrating LINCS to secure AWS cloud servers, we can safeguard the privacy of data, accounts, and workloads for thousands of users and agency staff — while ensuring compliance with federal IT security requirements.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Technical fluidity</p><div class="body"><p>Improvements to technical architecture and the implementation of cutting edge DevOps practices have provided more flexibility for the LINCS systems. This results in rapid improvements and fewer limitations for the user community.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Streamlined content</p><div class="body"><p>Multiple, outdated websites are consolidated into a modern and streamlined experience for users. Practitioners can quickly find what they need among the vast resources provided by the Department of Education through LINCS.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Valuable partnership</p><div class="body"><p>Our ongoing work with the Department of Education is a model of true agile partnership. We collaborate with an active and engaged Product Owner who advocates for the agency’s priorities as we work to make them a reality.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>CivicActions, along with our partner <a href="https://fearless.tech/">Fearless</a>,  facilitated Drupal 10 upgrades across the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) suite of websites, bringing improvements for editors, better security and accessibility, and community contributions to streamline upgrades for large- scale Drupal. The new Claro administration theme is cleaner, clearer, and more accessible.</p>
<p>The new rich text editor CKEditor 5 provides many UI enhancements and an improved user experience. The most significant change from previous versions of CKEditor is that editors must now use a predefined set of elements to configure the content, which leads to fewer instances of invalid markup patterns making their way into the published site. Since invalid or non-semantic markup is often the cause of accessibility issues, this is a major upgrade.  In addition, the improved Layout Builder experience makes it easier for content editors to control more complex layouts, while still keeping consistent with CMS Design System standards.</p>
<p>The 8 sites included in the upgrade, which occurred ahead of schedule, were: <a href="https://www.cms.gov/">CMS.gov</a>; <a href="https://www.medicare.gov/">Medicare.gov</a>; <a href="https://openpaymentsdata.cms.gov/">Openpaymentsdata.cms.gov</a>; <a href="https://data.medicaid.gov/">Data.medicaid.gov</a>; <a href="https://data.healthcare.gov/">Data.healthcare.gov</a>; SDIS.medicaid.gov (internal CMS site); PFS.data.cms.gov (internal CMS site); QIC.cms.gov (internal CMS site); and <a href="https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/">Provider Data Catalog (data.cms.gov/provider-data)</a>.</p></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>

<li>Information Architecture</li>

<li>MVP rapid prototyping</li>
<li>CI/CD Pipeline development</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>

<li>Node.js</li>
<li>React</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">More Accessible Experience</p><div class="body"><p>The new Claro administration theme is cleaner, clearer, and more accessible. In addition, the shift to CKEditor5 decreases accessibility errors from invalid markup.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Better User Interface for Editors</p><div class="body"><p>The improved Layout Builder experience makes it easier for content editors to control more complex layouts, while still keeping consistent with CMS Design System standards.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Improved Human-Centered Design</p><div class="body"><p>Drupal 10’s new rich text editor CKEditor 5 provides many UI enhancements and an improved user experience.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Better than On Time</p><div class="body"><p>This work was completed before the deadline and included upgrades on eight websites for CMS, meaning more improvements sooner.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Improved Security</p><div class="body"><p>Drupal 10’s upgraded Symfony 6 allows for increased security, so site users can feel secure that their data is private.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Seamless Transition</p><div class="body"><p>With zero downtime class="inner"><h1>Building a modern web experience for FCC customers</h1><span class="client-name">Federal Communications Commission</span><p class="body">In a fast-paced, comprehensive content migration, we applied Agile development and DevSecOps to modernize a legacy federal website.</p></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">69,706</h2><p class="body stat--text">pieces of migrated content</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">15</h2><p class="body stat--text">minutes for daily agile scrum meetings</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">19</h2><p class="body stat--text">bureaus and offices housed within FCC</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“This work will make it easier for both content owners to keep pages updated and for website users to navigate the website and find information.” </p><p class="body source">Dr. David Bray | FCC Chief Information Officer (public news release from FCC)</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) relies on its website to provide regulatory guidance to millions of visitors across various industries. But the old site was hard for users to navigate and frustrating for employees to manage.</p>
<p>In this rapid engagement, CivicActions worked hand-in-hand with the FCC to build a modern, mobile-friendly Drupal website that was more accessible and easier to update.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>The FCC’s cumbersome, outdated site was not doing its users or internal content managers  justice. On top of antiquated technology, the Commission's waterfall processes made it harder for content managers to keep the site updated and relevant for its diverse audiences. The policies and the product needed a refresh.</p>
<ul>
<li>Transition from waterfall to Agile methodology</li>
<li>Migrate legacy content from various systems to a modern Drupal Content Management System (CMS)</li>
<li>Ease public access to regulatory information through a mobile-friendly web experience</li>
<li>Save FCC administrators time and money with more efficient content management</li>
<li>Provide reliability and stability by implementing Quality Assurance (QA) testing</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Content Migration & Consolidation</li>
<li>Security Compliance</li>
<li>DevSecOps</li>
<li>Mobile Optimization</li>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Content Strategy</li>
<li>Responsive Design</li>
<li>Agile Implementation & Training</li>
<li>Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Drupal 6 to 7 (migration)</li>
<li>Custom Third-Party Integrations</li>
<li>Behat</li>
<li>Pa11y</li>
<li>WAVE</li>
<li>Accessibility Developer Tools</li>
<li>Mapbox</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>We had to work fast and our deployment options were limited by security considerations, so we rolled up our sleeves and turned up the collaboration. By implementing a modern Drupal CMS and Agile practices, we helped the FCC modernize its approach to content while avoiding disruptions for users and maintaining a secure environment.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Seamless content migration and management</h3><div class="body"><p>FCC has a very active user community, so we had to move quickly and avoid disruptions. We performed a massive content migration from Drupal 6 to Drupal 7 and consolidated content from various legacy systems into one CMS. To make the content creation and editing more pleasant and efficient, we added a robust text editor and new access controls. This allowed FCC’s many content creators to manage their own content without compromising the integrity of the site’s design.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/FCC_1_2a1f2981d3/FCC_1_2a1f2981d3.jpg" alt="Person using a laptop to access the redesigned FCC.gov."><div class="caption">The modernized FCC.gov is clean, simple, and easy to use for visitors and agency staff.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Accessible content</h3><div class="body"><p>The FCC is responsible for the accessibility of 21st Century communications, so there was no room for accessibility errors on its website. We scanned the site for compliance issues and quickly resolved them. The current website serves as a model for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and complies with Section 508 requirements.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/FCC_2_70dd211527/FCC_2_70dd211527.jpg" alt="FCC website displayed on a mobile device."><div class="caption">The mobile-optimized user experience lets people do business with FCC from anywhere.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Automatic testing for quality code</h3><div class="body"><p>Knowing that government websites can be subject to degradation over time as new code is added, we also wanted to help FCC achieve sustainability for their site.  We used Behat—a behavior-driven development testing framework that can double as user acceptance test criteria—to make sure all new code worked properly. We configured Behat tests to run automatically whenever new code was merged, ensuring a quality codebase for years to come.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Improved practices for better staff experience</h3><div class="body"><p>The content editors at FCC  were drowning in waterfall processes that didn’t let them respond quickly to evolving needs at the agency. To ease content management and improve the employee experience, we worked with key stakeholders to implement Agile practices. Together we curated priorities, made sure the end result met real user needs, and helped the FCC transition to ways of working better suited to the digital age.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/FCC_3_958d1aaef3/FCC_3_958d1aaef3.jpg" alt="Diagram showing the complex ways that information is authored and published at FCC."><div class="caption">An effective web modernization requires a deep understanding of content workflows.</div></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Smooth transition</p><div class="body"><p>We performed a massive content migration and consolidation with no disruption to the FCC user community.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Designed for usability</p><div class="body"><p>The improved site search and intuitive navigation help visitors quickly find information and resources published by the Commission.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Simplified content management</p><div class="body"><p>FCC content creators are equipped with a powerful text editor to update and manage their content without compromising the integrity of the site design.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Accessible for all people</p><div class="body"><p>We scanned for compliance issues and made sure the FCC site is usable for people of varying abilities, including those using assistive or mobile technology.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Sustainable, quality code</p><div class="body"><p>By implementing  automated testing software that scans all new code merges, we set the FCC up for long-term success with code quality baked-in.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Turn-key deployment</p><div class="body"><p>Deployment was complicated due to security, so we developed turn-key processes to deploy to production so the IT folks at FCC could do it themselves.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Let’s build a public success story.</h2><span class="inner"><h1>Using open data to power Georgia’s healthcare workforce</h1><span class="client-name">Georgia Board of Health Care Workforce</span><p class="body">Using the DKAN open source open data platform, we built tools to help Georgia decision-makers plan for a resilient healthcare workforce.</p></div></section><section class="case-study--hero-image"><div class="inner"><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/GBHCW_hero_ef1aadb6b9/GBHCW_hero_ef1aadb6b9.png" alt="A picture of a black laptop computer showing colorful pie charts displaying Georgia's healthcare data, such as physician distribution by age, and physicians retiring within the next five years."><span class="caption">The dashboards are searchable by county and by practitioner type.</span></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">10.5M </h2><p class="body stat--text">Georgians served by healthcare data </p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">159 </h2><p class="body stat--text">counties represented</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">20</h2><p class="body stat--text">published articles promoting the data visualization tool </p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“This collaboration birthed the interactive workforce analysis tool which — for the first time in the State — allowed legislators and workforce advocates to view healthcare workforce data online for free.”</p><p class="body source">Leanna Greenwood | Senior Data Analyst, GBHCW</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The <a href="https://healthcareworkforce.georgia.gov/">Georgia Board of Health Care Workforce (GBHCW)</a> serves communities in the state with a focus on medically underserved areas. The agency provides data reports on the physician, physician assistant, and nurse workforce and funds loan repayment programs to recruit healthcare workers to underserved parts of the state. However, healthcare workforce planners were having trouble estimating and meeting demand for practitioners across counties --especially as the COVID-19 pandemic drew many of them out of Georgia and into various hotspot states. Additionally, without publicly-available data on healthcare workers, GBHCW struggled to inform medical facilities with potential funding and staffing needs."</p>
<p>The agency saw an opportunity to leverage the <a href="https://getdkan.org/">DKAN</a> open data platform where they were already hosting their data, combined with custom data services from our team. We worked with GBHCW to create data visualizations and tools that make it easy for staff, medical practitioners, and the public to access the information needed to build a resilient and responsive state healthcare workforce.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>We were tasked with crafting detailed, easy-to-read visualizations for data provided by the Georgia Composite Medical Board and the Georgia Board of Nursing. We also built robust, <a href="https://data.georgia.gov/dashboard/physician">multifunctional dashboards</a> that allow data to be searched across physicians, physician assistants, and nurses. The dashboards needed to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Host and display data resources with user needs in mind</li>
<li>Show the number of licensed healthcare practitioners in a given area</li>
<li>Display data in a clear, user-friendly, and accessible way</li>
<li>Be easily adaptable and sustainable with the constant influx of new data</li>
<li>Reflect diverse intersections within the data (gender, race, qualifications, etc.)</li>
<li>Help legislators make data-based decisions to improve the healthcare field</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Data Visualization & Dashboards</li>
<li>Informed Research Methods</li>
<li>Data Cataloguing</li>
<li>Helpdesk Support</li>
<li>Visual Design</li>
<li>Data Maintenance</li>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Content Strategy</li>
<li>API Design & Deployment</li>
<li>Agile Methodologies</li>
<li>Data Tidying</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>DKAN/DKAN2</li>
<li>React</li>
<li>D3.js</li>
<li>Google Analytics</li>
<li>Vega</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>Because other state agencies were already using the open source <a href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.drupal.org/industries/government&sa=D&source=editors&ust=1623712161037000&usg=AOvVaw0Ai1Lgtnk5AgBmV1udMzGh">Drupal</a> framework to publish and manage government content, GBHCW chose the Drupal-based open data platform <a href="https://getdkan.org/">DKAN</a> for their data dashboards. The agency also saved time and money by utilizing an existing contract with us, adding new digital products to pre-built infrastructure.</p>
<p>As the core maintainers of DKAN, we provided research-based recommendations and custom data design and development services to make sure the dashboards solved the right problems for agency staff and stakeholders.  The project was so successful that the client reached out to us with the intent to create more dashboards to display patient care and underserved areas data.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Build for real user needs</h3><div class="body"><p>We brought a human-centered approach to the data dashboards, and used the <a href="https://reactjs.org/">React.js</a> library to build intuitive visualizations. We listened carefully to the desired outcomes, researched user needs, then made suggestions for how people could best learn about the demographic makeup and overall distribution of physicians, physician assistants, and nurses throughout the state.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/GBHCW_1_026d791b0d/GBHCW_1_026d791b0d.png" alt="A bar chart showing Georgia's numbers for physicians who accept Medicaid."><div class="caption">User research helped us identify the kinds of data people are seeking, and how best to display it.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Deliver early and often</h3><div class="body"><p>For the redesign of the data dashboards, we used agile sprint cycles with daily stand-up meetings to develop and implement small chunks of working software quickly. We used test data provided by GBHCW to create proofs-of-concept, with graphs and charts that made sense of the various elements we knew the client wanted to showcase.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/GBHCW_2_71ab09aeca/GBHCW_2_71ab09aeca.jpg" alt="An image of a flow chart showing the different stages of an agile development cycle."><div class="caption">Our team of developers and product specialists used agile sprint cycles to produce high-quality deliverables at regular intervals</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Align and adapt</h3><div class="body"><p>Meeting regularly with project leaders at the agency ensured that the vision and work remained in alignment. Together we reviewed work that had been done, checked if adjustments were needed, and responded quickly to evolving requests or new data. Staying in close communication ensured there were no surprises and the client goals were met.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Modern, accessible data</p><div class="body"><p>Instead of having to address time-consuming data requests, agency staff can quickly refer people to the live dashboards. Data updates and maintenance are quick and simple, saving time and money for GBHCW.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Serving vulnerable populations</p><div class="body"><p>People can view the workforce data by county, specialty, and other identifiers. These geographical differentiations help policymakers and stakeholders identify and remedy gaps in rural health coverage.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Reliable data analysis</p><div class="body"><p>The state of Georgia once relied on unpredictable volunteer efforts for analysis of nursing workforce data. Instead, the dashboards see regular analytics and data presentations formalized into existing processes.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Sustainable framework</p><div class="body"><p>The agency leveraged an existing open data contract with us, which meant we could utilize the web-based resources needed to make this effort sustainable and efficient for years to come.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Increased resilience</p><div class="body"><p>Easy access to data is critical during public health emergencies, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. From awareness campaigns to vaccination efforts, the agency is better prepared to mobilize its health workforce.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Data for public use</p><div class="body"><p>The dashboards allow anyone to easily observe workforce trends and create evidence-based initiatives in service of the public, including journalists, nonprofits, advocacy groups, or pharmaceutical vendors.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Let’s build a public success story.</h2><span class="h3">Get in touch to start.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/contact/">Put us to work</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/careers/">Join our team</a></div></div></section></div></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><h1>A smoother path to scientific research and discovery</h1><span class="client-name">The National Science Foundation</span><p class="body">Using human-centered design and the latest Drupal technology, we helped NSF build a dynamic website to advance their mission.</p></div></section><section class="case-study--hero-image"><div class="inner"><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/NSF_hero_814592da8e/NSF_hero_814592da8e.png" alt=""></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">25</h2><p class="body stat--text">stakeholder design review cycles</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">350+</h2><p class="body stat--text">user research participants from over 60 organizations</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">2,000+</h2><p class="body stat--text">deployments and completed Jira tickets</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“A few small changes in the approach saved hours and hours of Drupal development. There’s no silos. There’s no delay. When something comes through the UX process it has a developer stamp of approval.”</p><p class="body source">Kristian Ducharme | Team Technical Lead, CivicActions</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The National Science Foundation (NSF) is an independent federal agency created by Congress in 1950 to “promote the progress of science” and “advance the national health, prosperity, and welfare." With a 2021 budget of $8.5 billion, NSF accounts for over 25 percent of the total research funds awarded at U.S. colleges and universities.</p>
<p>CivicActions was tasked with rebuilding the entire public-facing NSF website, including implementation of all new visuals and improvement of the information architecture. By collaborating closely with stakeholders across NSF and adopting a rapid-iteration MVP approach, we regularly released prioritized features while simultaneously building the back-end infrastructure to power the ongoing full-scale migration.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>To better serve employees and the scientific community — including researchers in mathematics, computer science, social sciences, and beyond — NSF needed to replace the existing NSF.gov with a modern, flexible, cloud-hosted online experience. Primary goals were to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Modernize and improve the user experience for nsf.gov</li>
<li>Improve funding search for colleges, researchers, and scientists</li>
<li>Empower NSF staff with a new Content Management System (CMS)</li>
<li>Leverage user research and testing throughout the project</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>UX Research</li>
<li>UX Design</li>
<li>Visual Design</li>
<li>Drupal Development</li>
<li>AWS Cloud Hosting Architecture Design</li>
<li>DevOps Architecture / Support</li>
<li>Project Management</li>
<li>Drupal Training</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Drupal 8 / 9</li>
<li>Sandbox mimics production</li>
<li>AirTable</li>
<li>Sketch</li>
<li>Invision</li>
<li>Mural</li>
<li>SAML Authentication</li>
<li>Patternlab / U.S. Web Design System</li>
<li>Docker</li>
<li>Kubernetes AWS EKS / RDS /  ElasticSearch / S3</li>
<li>Drupal Layout Builder, Groups</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>To support timelines for a public launch, we took an “MVP approach” by launching a beta site with a small, prioritized set of functionalities. As new pages and features are built, the site continues to develop over time, in the open. This approach requires rapid prototyping and iteration, frequent testing, and continuous engagement with stakeholders.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Start by understanding the needs</h3><div class="body"><p>After some initial design discovery, NSF engaged CivicActions in September of 2018 to begin a site-wide redesign and migration. The legacy NSF.gov site — built mostly in static HTML —  was hard to manage and laborious to update. We knew a scalable, flexible CMS solution was needed, so we got right to work on development and design — starting the site infrastructure, building the initial set of components, and kicking off design research.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/NSF_1_b61a326fd8/NSF_1_b61a326fd8.png" alt="A colorful pie chart showing the various tasks that users of the NSF website need to accomplish."><div class="caption">Identifying “top tasks” of various user groups helps us solve the right problems for people.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Deliver fast and improve continually</h3><div class="body"><p>By the spring of 2019, we’d launched <a href="https://beta.nsf.gov/">beta.nsf.gov</a> and established an iterative, MVP-based approach that allowed our design and development team to release and test content with static data while continuing to build out the site infrastructure. Later that year, we released an updated Careers portal on <a href="https://beta.nsf.gov/careers">https://beta.nsf.gov/careers</a>, and began research on the Funding portal and the Funding Search feature.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/NSF_2_47110bd4c6/NSF_2_47110bd4c6.png" alt="A person viewing NSF career opportunities on a mobile device."><div class="caption">The new Careers page makes it easier for the nation’s top scientific talent to find opportunities at NSF.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Improve organizational processes</h3><div class="body"><p>Working closely with NSF stakeholders, we continued to steadily test and release features, launching the <a href="https://beta.nsf.gov/science-matters">Science Matters blog</a> and an updated top level menu in February 2020. By the fall, we integrated the Pims Rest API to streamline NSF’s online program management, and deployed the Drupal Layout Builder tool that allows content editors to drag and drop content as they build and publish pages.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/NSF_3_172c49dd2d/NSF_3_172c49dd2d.png" alt="Screenshot of the Layout Builder module in Drupal, showing how content editors can drag-and-drop sections."><div class="caption">Content editors at NSF get their jobs done faster and better using Layout Builder in Drupal.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Partnership for public good</h3><div class="body"><p>In 2021, after extensive research, testing and iteration, the updated Funding Search Portal will be launched in June — creating a simpler, quicker way to fund the research that powers the U.S. scientific community.  Additionally that year, CivicActions was awarded a $44 million contract extension to continue supporting this important work. As we look to the future with a growing team and ambitious goals, we are grateful for our ongoing partnership with NSF.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Fast delivery of value</p><div class="body"><p>Our “MVP approach” helped NSF launch their new site sooner, with ongoing improvements being made in the open. Public feedback is welcome along the way.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Ongoing Drupal upgrades</p><div class="body"><p>As we continue to migrate the site, we will scan all modules for deprecated code, contribute patches to Drupal.org, refactor theming for Twig 2 compatibility, and perform core updates to Drupal 9.x.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Automated testing</p><div class="body"><p>To check the updated codebase for failures and disrupted user paths, we run automated tests including accessibility scanners, security, unit testing, behavioral testing, and code quality.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Confident deployments</p><div class="body"><p>Through 73 sprints, 2,000 deployments, and over 2,000 Jira tickets, the abundance of automation and testing gives us confidence in our code.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Research-based solution</p><div class="body"><p>Because NSF invested in broad user research and testing, they can be confident that their new site meets the real needs of the scientific community and the organization stakeholders.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Taxpayer savings</p><div class="body"><p>The intuitive new content management system allows NSF staff to publish and update helpful information quickly and easily. The time they’re saving can be reinvested into other mission-critical work.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--staff"><div class="inner"><h2>Meet the team</h2><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Monday, March 2, 2020
<strong>Lafayette, Calif.</strong> - The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services on Feb. 28 awarded CivicActions a $18.25 million contract for Web Experience and Content Management Services (WECMS), according to USASpending.gov.</p>
<p>The contract calls for a redesign of CMS.gov and Medicare.gov, as well as migrating the agency’s open data portals to new sites using DKAN, a free and open source open data platform.</p>
<p>The digital services agency, which started in 2004, specializes in user centered design, Drupal development, security and compliance, open data, and DevOps. CivicActions is also the core maintainer of DKAN.</p>
<p>The contract starts on March 2, 2020 and has two, one-year options to extend the project to June 1, 2023, up to a total of $18.25M.</p>
<p>Earlier this year, the firm was named to the GovTech Top 100 list for the fourth year in a row.</p>
<p>CivicActions is also a founding member of the Digital Services Coalition, a group of 16 companies dedicated to bringing the innovation and agility that has become the backbone of commercial digital services to the government.</p>
<p>For this contract, CivicActions is partnering with Fearless, another Digital Services Coalition member firm, in a Contractor Teaming Arrangement.
<a href="https://www.usaspending.gov/#/award/CONT_AWD_75FCMC20F0025_7530_GS35F337BA_4732">Award information on USASpending.gov</a></p></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><h1>CivicActions Certified to Deliver DITAP Training to Federal Acquisition Professionals</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Friday, August 14, 2020</p>
<p><strong>Lafayette, Calif.</strong> - CivicActions has been officially certified as a FAC-C-DS Core Plus Training Provider to deliver modern digital service procurement education and training to federal contracting officers, according to the <a href="https://techfarhub.cio.gov/initiatives/ditap/">TechFAR Hub</a>.</p>
<p>The training is part of the Digital IT Acquisition Professional (DITAP) initiative, an effort by the U.S. Digital Service (USDS) and the Office of Federal Procurement Policy to equip contracting officers with the knowledge and skills to make smart IT purchasing decisions and lead innovation in government digital services acquisitions within the constraints of current federal procurement practices.</p>
<p>Starting in 2022, all federal acquisition professionals managing contracts of $7 million or greater will be required to have FAC-C-DS certification, reflecting their understanding of modern digital service procurement. The training will be available through approved vendors or the Federal Acquisition Institute. CivicActions is the second company to become a certified vendor of the training, following the joint development of the curriculum by USDS and global consulting firm ICF.</p>
<p>CivicActions specializes in services that are central to the DITAP curriculum such as human centered design, free and open source software development, security and compliance, Agile and Lean Startup methodologies, and DevOps. By helping acquisition professionals align their contracting processes with these practices through which modern software is built, the DITAP program aims to increase the number and percentage of successful digital service acquisitions across the federal government.</p>
<p>Over the past 18 months, CivicActions has trained three cohorts of acquisition professionals, encompassing more than 70 learners from 20 different federal agencies. 100% of participants reported “clear takeaways from the course” and 92% would recommend the training to a colleague. DITAP alumni will continue to be supported by others in the acquisition community as leaders for change within their organizations.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://civicactions.com/services/ditap">Request DITAP training</a></li>
<li>Reflections on DITAP: <a href="https://medium.com/civicactions/what-we-learned-from-training-procurement-officers-to-buy-modern-government-it-cc6309df4103">What we learned from training procurement officers to buy modern government IT</a></li>
<li>Learn more about DITAP at the <a href="https://techfarhub.cio.gov/initiatives/ditap/">TechFAR Hub</a></li>
</ul></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><h1>CivicActions Expands Accessibility Capabilities With OpenConcept</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Monday, November 9, 2020
<strong>Lafayette, Calif.</strong> – <a href="https://civicactions.com">CivicActions</a>, a professional services firm modernizing government technologies and services, today announced it has acquired <a href="https://openconcept.ca/drupal">OpenConcept</a>, a development firm specializing in web accessibility through open source tools and community.</p>
<p>“CivicActions creates digital services that work for everyone, and that means people of all abilities,” said Owen Barton, Director of Engineering at CivicActions. “By having OpenConcept join us, we’re strengthening our capacity to help government agencies innovate in ways that are inclusive from the onset.”</p>
<p>Both CivicActions and OpenConcept are longtime providers of and contributors to Drupal, an open source content management platform that helps organizations meet accessibility standards as they evolve. Specifically, Drupal supports compliance with the newly-updated Section 508, a law requiring federal agencies to make their information and communication technology (ICT) accessible to people of varying abilities.</p>
<p>“People tend to think of web accessibility as a checklist — but the web is now evolving so quickly that today’s checklist could be outdated next year,” said OpenConcept founder Mike Gifford, who will now serve as a Senior Strategist at CivicActions, advising on and identifying opportunities for improving accessibility compliance in government.</p>
<p>“Web accessibility must be part of the foundational design, and CivicActions is emerging as a leader in this space,” Gifford said. “My team and I are thrilled to further amplify that work and help government agencies raise the bar in building simple, inclusive services for citizens.”</p>
<p>Visit the company blog to read more about how CivicActions is <!-- --><a class='external-link' href='https://medium.com/civicactions/4-ways-to-improve-government-accessibility-through-open-source-8e20fabc7281'><!-- -->improving government accessibility through open source.<!-- --></a><!-- --> To speak with someone about CivicActions’ services, please send an email to <a href="mailto:contact@civicactions.com">contact@civicactions.com</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Contact</strong></p>
<p>Marlena Medford, Marketing & Content Strategist</p>

class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: May 3, 2021
<a href="https://civicactions.com">CivicActions</a> is pleased to announce that the National Science Foundation (NSF) has <a href="https://etc.g2xchange.com/statics/small-business-scores-44m-nsf-web-content-management-system-cms-support-contract">awarded us a 5-year contract</a> at $44M to continue working with the agency using human-centered and agile approaches to improve how their website serves the scientific community.</p>
<p>This will include further improvement of NSF’s web content management system (CMS) through human-centered development, modernization, and enhancement (DME); and ongoing operations and maintenance (O&M). We are delighted to help support the agency’s mission of advancing scientific research and discovery applied to practical problems.</p>
<p>Our work is slated to begin in spring 2021. This work was awarded through our General Services Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract.</p>
<p>Our previous work with NSF has taken a research-based approach to the redesign and modernization of the agency’s website, including the design and development of an improved search feature that easily connects science researchers with opportunities to obtain funding for their work.</p>
<p>To learn more about how we’re advancing public service, read our <a href="https://civicactions.com/case-studies">latest case studies</a>.</p></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: May 11, 2021</p>
<p><a href="https://civicactions.com">CivicActions</a> is pleased to announce that the Department of Education has awarded us an $8.1M contract to continue supporting its Literacy and Information Communication System (LINCS), which helps adult learners prepare for 21st century jobs.</p>
<p>This 5-year contract was awarded through our General Services Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract. Work is slated to begin in spring 2021. Under this contract we will maintain, develop, enhance, and update the LINCS websites, web-based tools, databases, database search engines, streaming media, and content management and learning management systems.</p>
<p>These systems support the work of a varied ecosystem of educational instructors, administrative leaders, researchers, curriculum developers, and learners. Modern technology is key to their success, and we are proud to apply agile and human-centered methodologies to the improvement of the platforms they rely on for learning and cross-agency collaboration.</p>
<p>Our previous work with the Department of Education has resulted in a fruitful partnership through which we provided consolidation and improvement of LINCS websites, DevOps processes for continuous testing and releasing, and friendly helpdesk support integrated with agile workflows for a truly user-centered process.</p>
<p>To learn more about how we’re advancing public service, read our <a href="https://civicactions.com/case-studies">latest case studies</a>.</p></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt.
