class="inner"><h1>GSA Engages CivicActions to Modernize VPAT to Improve Digital Accessibility</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Thursday, July 8, 2021</p>
<p>CivicActions is excited to announce a new contract with General Services Administration (GSA) to reimagine the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template® (VPAT®) into a modernized format to support better accessibility for digital products.</p>
<p>The VPAT currently exists as a lengthy Word document that lists accessibility requirements for technology products, such as software and hardware. It’s often used by vendors during the proposal process to demonstrate the accessibility of their digital products — but the outdated format of the VPAT hinders its effectiveness.</p>
<p>CivicActions will help the GSA convert its VPAT to a machine-readable format, called the Open Product Accessibility Template (OPAT). This will be an open standard used by vendors to produce compliance reports just as they do currently with VPAT — but with the improved template, the reports will be in structured digital files that are easier to validate and update.</p>
<p>This work will result in:</p>
<ul>
<li>Better understanding of the accessibility of digital products</li>
<li>Stronger consideration for accessibility in procurement processes</li>
<li>Easier management of accessibility reporting by agency staff in accordance with best practices</li>
</ul>
<p>GSA is setting a new standard for making digital accessibility a meaningful part of IT procurement. We are proud to be part of this work, which will lead to building government digital services that better serve people of all abilities.</p>
<p>To learn more about how we’re advancing accessibility in government, visit our <a href="https://accessibility.civicactions.com/">Accessibility Community of Practice</a>.</p>
<p>More on this topic</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://gcn.com/articles/2021/02/04/accessibility-compliance-as-code.aspx">The need for accessibility compliance as code</a></li>
<li><a href="https://medium.com/civicactions/4-ways-to-improve-government-accessibility-through-open-source-8e20fabc7281">How open source tools improve accessibility for government</a></li>
<li><a href="https://medium.com/civicactions/whitehouse-gov-makes-an-accessibility-statement-5de37580209">Accessibility initiatives from the White House</a></li>
</ul></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><h1>Better transit service with real-time data</h1><span class="client-name">New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority</span><p class="body">Wrangling a vast network of real-time transit data, we used Drupal 8 and the Internet of Things to modernize digital subway signage in New York City.</p></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">5.7 M</h2><p class="body stat--text">Riders using real time info every day</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number"> 1800</h2><p class="body stat--text">New clocks added in 400 subway stations</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">3,000+ </h2><p class="body stat--text">Unique digital signs connected with AWS Internet of Things</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“CivicActions engineers were able to carry through complex technical requirements so that an entire city's worth of data could be captured, parsed, and displayed in a matter of a few seconds.”</p><p class="body source">Mike Madison, Senior Technical Architect, Acquia</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The Metropolitan Transit Authority (MTA) manages the world’s largest public transit system, helping over 11 million passengers get around New York City every day. The data universe is complex and constantly changing, representing a massive network of trains, tracks, and stations — which need to display reliably and in real time to keep riders informed.
Acquia and CivicActions worked with MTA to extend the agency’s existing Drupal content management system (CMS) to a network of devices using Amazon’s Internet of Things (IoT). We helped MTA set the modern standard for using digital signage to communicate train arrival times, weather info, and service updates — making it easier for riders to plan their routes and get there on time.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>Riders rely on station signs and the MTA’s website for travel information to help them know when their train will arrive. To better inform riders in real time, MTA needed a way to display information from their website on digital signs in subway stations and platforms.</p>
<ul>
<li>Improve travel experience for subway riders by providing  up-to-date info</li>
<li>Empower MTA administrators to easily manage data on a familiar platform</li>
<li>Provide real time data to help modernize public transportation</li>
<li>Implement a flexible system to accommodate future growth</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Technical Leadership Consulting</li>
<li>Technical Architecture Development</li>
<li>User Research</li>
<li>Design Thinking and Application</li>
<li>Interface Design</li>
<li>Backend Development Expertise</li>
<li>Design Implementation</li>
<li>Content Modeling</li>
<li>Responsive Design</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Decoupled Drupal 8</li>
<li>React.js</li>
<li>Amazon Internet of Things (IoT)</li>
<li>PHPUnit / Jest (unit testing)</li>
<li>Acquia Build and Launch Tool (BLT)</li>
<li>MQTT Messaging Protocol</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>To better serve their customers and set their employees up for success, the MTA needed a single administrative site that could manage a lot of data from a variety of external feeds. Drupal 8 was a natural choice for the CMS because it can seamlessly integrate data from all these sources.</p>
<p>Then we connected over 3,000 MTA digital screens as unique devices on a private and secure “Internet of Things” within Amazon Web Services — allowing Drupal to push location-specific data to each individual screen. Read a <a href="https://dev.acquia.com/blog/using-drupal-8-and-aws-iot-to-power-digital-signage-for-new-yorks-subway-system/01/10/2018/20051">technical deep-dive on this work</a> from our partner.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Decoupled approach for flexibility</h3><div class="body"><p>The MTA needed to display data reliably regardless of the device or front-end design. We created a custom decoupled (headless) Drupal theme built in React.js to adapt to different screen sizes and mobile platforms. The decoupled backend continually evaluates and pushes data from a variety of web service APIs, while compensating for incomplete or outdated information, so users only see data that’s relevant to them.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/MTA_1_5da100cebc/MTA_1_5da100cebc.jpg" alt="A man in a suit stands outside the entrance to the 5th Avenue Bryant Park Metro station in New York City, holding a closed laptop at his side and in his left hand, while he browses his smartphone with his right hand. "><div class="caption">Real time data, viewable from any device, lets subway riders know when their train will arrive. (Photo by Ketut Subiyanto from Pexels)</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Content modeling for data management</h3><div class="body"><p>To help MTA staff manage the flow of data, we created a digital representation — a content model — of the routes, stations, platforms, tracks, and signs throughout the system. This helped us break large data sets into smaller, actionable components so the right information can be served up in the right context.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/MTA_2_d34e1d1f38/MTA_2_d34e1d1f38.png" alt="A diagram showing the content model CivicActions developed and which illustrates the flow of data from the routes, stations, platforms, tracks, and signs throughout the subway system."><div class="caption">Content model features allow the MTA to control data streams across the subway system.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Open source for cost savings</h3><div class="body"><p>By using open source technology instead of expensive proprietary software, we helped the MTA lower costs and avoid vendor lock-in. Open source software like Drupal also offers a more flexible web-publishing approach than complex legacy solutions. Additionally, an open source approach can help agencies ensure <a href="https://medium.com/civicactions/4-ways-to-improve-government-accessibility-through-open-source-8e20fabc7281">better web accessibility</a> for the long term.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/MTA_3_6b3db3892a/MTA_3_6b3db3892a.png" alt="Graphic showing how information is sent along the system from the agency to the devices of end users."><div class="caption">The new system allows MTA to send real time data to hundreds of digital signs simultaneously.</div></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label"> Timely digital data</p><div class="body"><p>With over 3,000 unique digital signs connected to AWS Internet of Things, MTA helps customers see data that is timely and specific to their location and needs.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Easy administration</p><div class="body"><p>We developed a Drupal 8 content model to support the MTA’s administrative dashboard so even non-technical users can make changes themselves.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">React-ing in real time</p><div class="body"><p>Using <a href="https://reactjs.org/">React</a> allowed us to interpret incoming data, implement appropriate templates, and display relevant information throughout the system — no matter the screen or interface.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Simple workflows</p><div class="body"><p>The resilient “headless” approach allows MTA staff to use standard publishing workflows to manage data independently of the screens that are visible to end users.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Built-in resilience</p><div class="body"><p>A few seconds can make a big difference when navigating the world’s largest subway network. We made sure the system could compensate for internet lapses to keep data flowing in real time.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Room to grow</p><div class="body"><p>We simplified the front-end architecture to push data from a central location to a huge number of devices, so MTA can scale the system to accommodate signs for the entire network as it changes and grows.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Let’s build a public success story.</h2><span class="h3">Get in touch to start.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/contact/">Put us to work</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/careers/">Join our team</a></div></div></section></div></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><h1>CivicActions announces 24 DITAP graduates from the Department of Veterans Affairs</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Monday, July 19, 2021</p>
<p>CivicActions is pleased to announce the graduation of its newest <a href="https://civicactions/services/ditap">Digital IT Acquisition Professional (DITAP)</a> cohort, which included 24 procurement officers from the Department of Veteran Affairs.</p>
<p>DITAP was created to modernize how the federal government buys digital services. Specifically, it teaches students how to build flexible contracts that keep pace with changing technologies.</p>
<p>The six-month program starts by covering 21st century digital services — including agile software development, human-centered design, cloud computing and data management. Students then learn how to contract these services, and ensure their projects are successful.</p>
<p>DITAP also enables contracting officers to be business advisors and change agents within their own agencies. This serves DITAP’s bigger goal of building a culture of innovative acquisition across the federal government.</p>
<p>Upon DITAP graduation, students earn their Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting Core-Plus Specialization in Digital Services (<a href="https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/fac_c_digital_services_05_12_18.pdf?utm_medium=email&utm_source=govdelivery">FAC-C-DS</a>). By 2022, the FAC-C-DS will be required for all federal contracting officers who manage contracts of $7M or more.</p>
<p>With this cohort, CivicActions is pleased to congratulate the following DITAP graduates:</p>
<ul>
<li>Anthony Browner, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Camille Dye, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Chiffon Bradshaw, Procurement Analyst</li>
<li>Debra Bryce-Davis, Contract Specialist</li>

<li>John McDonnell, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Joshua Hammill, Contract Officer</li>
<li>Kalil O'Neal, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Kevin Andujar, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Mary Accomando, Supervisory Contracting Officer</li>
<li>Mary Beth Hall, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Michelle Policari, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Mina Awad, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Rene Brown, Procurement Analyst</li>
<li>Robert Robinson, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Sarah Bach, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Sharon Haywood, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Shreeia Curry, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Susan Meng, Management Analyst</li>
<li>Tasha Cheramie, Contract Specialist</li>
<li>Yash Dega, Contract Specialist</li>
</ul>
<p>CivicActions is proud to be the nation’s only small business that is fully-authorized  to provide DITAP training. class="inner"><h1>CivicActions Appoints Mike Gifford as Open Standards & Practices Lead, Expanding Commitment to an Open Ecosystem of Vendors and Agencies</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Tuesday, July 9, 2024</p>
<p>CivicActions, a leading provider of digital services to the Federal government, is proud to announce the appointment of Mike Gifford to the newly created position of Open Standards & Practices Lead. This strategic move underscores CivicActions' longstanding commitment to free and open source software, open data, and open practices in government digital services.</p>
<p>Since its founding twenty years ago in 2004, CivicActions has been at the forefront of advocating for and implementing open systems in the public sector. The creation of this new role formalizes the company's commitment to openness, transparency, and collaborative innovation in government technology.</p>
<p>Mike Gifford, formerly a Senior Strategist at CivicActions, brings extensive experience in open source technologies, accessibility, sustainability, and digital government practices to this role. As an internationally-recognized subject-matter expert, Gifford has been instrumental in shaping conversations around digital accessibility and open source solutions in the public sector.</p>
<p>In his new role, Mike Gifford will build upon his leadership in creating <a href="https://github.com/GSA/openacr">OpenACR (Open Accessibility Conformance Report)</a> for the US Federal General Services Agency (GSA). OpenACR aims to standardize and streamline the reporting of digital accessibility compliance. This effort was proposed as a <a href="https://civicactions.com/case-studies/open-acr/">concept to GSA</a> by CivicActions.</p>
<p>Gifford's vision extends beyond individual projects, focusing on collaborating on improving best practices with other firms, as well as fostering inter-agency open practices across Federal agencies. He will work to help create a more collaborative ecosystem where information and innovative approaches are freely shared and implemented. This approach not only aligns with CivicActions' commitment to openness, but also promises to accelerate the adoption of best practices in government technology, ultimately leading to more transparent, accessible, and effective public services.</p>
<p>Mike Gifford currently serves as the Board President of the <a href="https://digitalservicescoalition.org/#/">Digital Services Coalition (DSC)</a>, where he has been instrumental in sharing best practices and building a global community around delivering modern digital services.</p>
<p>Recent accolades further highlight Gifford's impact on the industry. He was recently named an <a href="https://www.govtechconnects.com/acquisition2024/">Acquisition Lifecycle Leadership Award Honoree</a> by GovTech Connects. Previously, he was recognized as a <a href="https://insights.govforum.io/2023/03/2023-change-agent-awardees-leaders-disrupting-the-federal-landscape-2/">2023 Disruptive Tech Change Agent</a> by FORUM (formerly FedHealthIT), underscoring his thought leadership in digital government. Additionally, the International Association of Accessibility Professionals (IAAP) honored him with the <a href="https://www.accessibilityassociation.org/s/iaap-awards#MGifford">2023 IAAP A11y Impact Award</a> for his significant contributions to the field of accessibility.</p>
<p>"After dedicating nearly 25 years to advancing free and open source software, I'm thrilled to step into a role that truly embodies the principles I've championed throughout my career," said Gifford. "Open standards, open source, open data, and open practices are not just buzzwords—they're the foundation for fostering collaboration, driving innovation, enhancing accessibility, and promoting sustainability in the digital realm. In this new position, I'm excited to lead our team in not only implementing these practices, but also in sharing and evolving best practices across the government sector. This role represents a unique opportunity to amplify the impact of open technologies and methodologies in creating more efficient, transparent, and inclusive digital services for all."</p>
<p>This appointment reflects CivicActions' ongoing mission to promote open knowledge as a cornerstone of effective, efficient, and transparent open government services. By investing in leadership focused on open standards and practices, CivicActions reaffirms its position as a pioneer in bringing the benefits of open source to the public sector.</p></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt. class="inner"><h1>Better Accessibility Through Alternative Text Validation</h1><span class="client-name">U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs</span><p class="body">We updated VA.gov based on user research to create better alternative (alt) text in order to provide a more accessible experience for Veterans.</p></div></section><section class="case-study--hero-image"><div class="inner"><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/va_1_101ba6383a/va_1_101ba6383a.png" alt="An image of a smiley face is displayed to show an example of inputting alt text on a VA website"></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">1053 </h2><p class="body stat--text">Drupal Editors</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">573</h2><p class="body stat--text"> Images uploaded per month (6 month average)</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">6</h2><p class="body stat--text">Mistakes prevented daily</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">"This is a phenomenal catch…I think something like this is a game changer.”</p><p class="body source">VA Drupal Editor </p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>Alternative text is a complex topic, as it is difficult to account for every possible scenario or to provide sufficient context for each image. However, in order for web pages to be the most accessible, any contextual images that have been added must include good quality, descriptive alt text.  Our team was tasked with updating the image upload editorial interface within Drupal to help editors add better, more useful alt text for the images they were uploading.</p>
<p>We completed a full, cross-disciplinary project with our partners <a href="https://www.friendsfromthecity.com/">Friends From The City</a> and <a href="https://agile6.com/">Agile Six</a>. The project included discovery to determine exactly which areas would be best to focus on, building a functional prototype for user research, and ultimately implementing improvements determined from that research to create a better, more informed user interface for Drupal editors.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>Our goal was to create a better alt text experience for Veterans visiting VA.gov. To achieve  this we had to improve the user interface within Drupal to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Streamline and simplify  the image upload form</li>
<li>Clearly identify the alternative text field</li>
<li>Add client-side validation for common errors seen within existing alt text</li>
<li>Provide clear and concise error messages for editors to correct mistakes</li>
<li>Educate  editors on how to create descriptive and accurate alt text and why it is important</li>
</ul></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Agile Methodologies</li>
<li>User Research</li>
<li>Prototype Development & Testing</li>
<li>Workflow & Interaction Design</li>
<li>Visual Design</li>
<li>Accessibility</li>
<li>Drupal Engineering</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Figma</li>
<li>Mural</li>
<li>Drupal</li>
<li>Google Sheets</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2></h2><div class="body"><p>Building on <a href="https://www.drupal.org/industries/government">Drupal</a>, an open-source content management system (CMS), we wanted to improve the image upload editorial interface by implementing guardrails to prevent poor quality alt text through the enforcement of accessibility best practices while also reducing frustrations for CMS editors who are writing the alt text - ultimately resulting in better quality alternative text for people who rely on it to access visual content on VA.gov.</p>
<p>Our team worked cross functionally with our partners to explore solutions that were not only technically feasible, but also solved a variety of user needs by following human centered design practices. Research was a key component to improving the alt text on VA.gov, from gathering and analyzing statistics on current alt text to conducting user research sessions. The final design that was implemented was a direct result of iteration based on user feedback and thought partnership with our team and the product owners at the VA.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Determine which metrics to target</h3><div class="body"><p>The current alt text for images within Drupal was evaluated based on multiple criteria - did the alt text contain a filename; was the alt text concise; was the alt text redundant; was the alt text accurate. The last criterion is very contextual, however the first three are more subjective and we decided to target those metrics to start focusing our improvements.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/va_2_1848f2c99b/va_2_1848f2c99b.png" alt="chart displaying cumulative trends in alt text quality"><div class="caption">For just over a year (September 2022 - November 2023), the percentage of images violating each of the targeted criteria for alt text has remained mostly consistent.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Identify Improvements</h3><div class="body"><p>We created an interactive prototype to test with users. We analyzed the feedback from those research sessions to determine the best way to incorporate validation into the alt text field with the least amount of user disruption. We also determined additional user interface updates that would make the entire image upload experience a simpler and easier task for the editor.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/va_1_7ea5f51049/va_1_7ea5f51049.png" alt="An image of a smiley face is displayed to show an example of inputting alt text on a VA website"></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Educate Drupal Editors</h3><div class="body"><p>We created training articles within the Drupal Knowledge Base to help editors contextualize alt text and more fully understand what it is and why it is important. By helping editors understand the experience a Veteran might have if an image they upload has poor alt text, they will better understand the content they need to provide to improve this experience.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/va_4_9416e44da9/va_4_9416e44da9.png" alt="Screenshot from VA.gov on Alternative Images guidelines"><div class="caption">Providing education and training articles for our editors allows them to complete their work more efficiently.</div></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Research-based design</p><div class="body"><p>We conducted research with VA.gov Drupal CMS editors to gather real data about how they upload images and interact with the alt text field. This data informed our final design decisions.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Improved editor interface</p><div class="body"><p>Our research found other improvements that could be made to the image upload user interface. These were small updates but resulted in a large impact to editors and greatly reduced confusion and frustration.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Immediate feedback</p><div class="body"><p>We added client-side validation to the alt text field,  providing feedback to editors immediately when an error occurs.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Targeted training materials</p><div class="body"><p>Education is a large part of making accessible content. We provided resources for editors to help them understand the importance of alt text, with examples that can help them create better content for people who may have a visual disability.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Scalability</p><div class="body"><p>The introduction of client-side validation allows for the expansion of this feature to other input fields of the Drupal CMS with similar content quality issues.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Accessible  information</p><div class="body"><p>VA.gov site visitors all deserve to access the information within the website. Providing better alt text allows the visual information in images to be available to those who may rely on a screen reader.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="inner"><h1>Helping Veterans access care and benefits online</h1><span class="client-name">U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs</span><p class="body">We joined the modernization effort at VA to implement a modern Drupal content management system and empower a Veteran-first approach to online healthcare.</p></div></section><section class="case-study--hero-image"><div class="inner"><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/VA_hero_46cae3d67f/VA_hero_46cae3d67f.png" alt="The redesigned VA medical center website displayed on a laptop and a mobile device"><span class="caption">Veterans can now manage their health care and benefits more easily online.</span></div></section><section class="section--case-study--stats"><div class="stats--wrapper"><div class="inner"><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">2,019</h2><p class="body stat--text">health services audited and consolidated</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">38</h2><p class="body stat--text">research sessions with VA content authors</p></div><div class="single-stat"><h2 class="stat--number">1 - 2</h2><p class="body stat--text">clicks on any device for Veterans to find what they need</p></div></div></div></section><div class="staff-quote quote first-quote no-img"><div class="inner"><div class="quote"><p class="h3">“VA is finally pivoting from focusing on its organizational structure to helping me as a Veteran.”</p><p class="body source">Veteran using the new VA.gov</p></div></div></div><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is working to improve the confusing experience many Veterans have when navigating multiple VA sites built on a mix of legacy technologies.</p>
<p>Having launched a reinvigorated VA.gov in 2018 as an important step to a unified Veteran-first digital platform, the agency still needed to build out a common content management system (CMS), establish consistent descriptions for services, and organize the information in an accessible way for Veterans in need of health care.</p></div></div><div class="goal"><h3>Client goal</h3><div class="body"><p>The large-scale pilot effort focused on using one of the regional VA Medical Centers as a model for all future VA.gov content. This would empower the VA to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Provide better healthcare management and scheduling online</li>
<li>Explain benefits clearly and provide intuitive paths to apply for them</li>
<li>Help minority and women Veterans find services specific to their needs</li>
<li>Provide online connection with care coordinators</li>
<li>Establish a model for content publishing and governance VA-wide</li>
</ul>
<p>We integrated the new CMS with the existing site architecture and helped create standards for content and design that make it easier for VA staff to do their jobs—while directly improving quality of life for millions of Veterans seeking health care and benefits.</p></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Usability testing</li>
<li>Data & Content Migration</li>
<li>Decoupled Methodology</li>
<li>User Research</li>
<li>Heuristic Evaluation</li>
<li>Persona & Scenario Design</li>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Content Strategy</li>
<li>Workflow & Interaction Design</li>
<li>Prototype Development & Testing</li>
<li>API Design & Deployment</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Decoupled Drupal 8</li>
<li>GraphQL</li>
<li>React</li>
<li>Metalsmith</li>
<li>U.S. Web Design System</li>
<li>Jenkins</li>
<li>Lando</li>
<li>AWS</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our approach</h2><div class="body"><p>Working alongside our partners <a href="https://agile6.com/">Agile Six</a> and <a href="https://www.navapbc.com/">Nava</a> in collaboration with the <a href="https://department-of-veterans-affairs.github.io/dsva/">U.S. Digital Service at VA</a> and other organizations, our team was one of many moving parts in a complex project. We provided technical leadership and modeled transparent communication practices that helped the various teams work effectively together.</p>
<p>The technical strategy shifted to a “decoupled” approach partway through the project, requiring us to integrate the new CMS backend with the VA’s existing frontend system so that Veterans and caregivers could access content across multiple platforms. Agile practices helped us navigate this and other evolving priorities in a large ecosystem undergoing significant changes.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Smooth the technical transition</h3><div class="body"><p>We managed the move to the new CMS without “pausing” the old site so the VA could re-use their existing front-end technology instead of starting from scratch. This meant we had to juggle content being served from two sources (GitHub and Drupal) during the transition, while training VA staff to use the new CMS effectively. We also set up a CI/CD pipeline for automated testing to ensure healthy functioning systems.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Find out what people need</h3><div class="body"><p>To make sure health services and benefits are easy to find and understand, we tested navigation and content with real people, including unique groups like women, minority, and LGBTQ Veterans. We also interviewed VA staff responsible for maintaining the website, to understand their pain points and develop authoring and approval processes that make their jobs easier.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/VA_2_160c4ebf95/VA_2_160c4ebf95.png" alt="Person using the updated VA medical center website on a mobile device"><div class="caption">The responsive, user-friendly interface makes it easy for Veterans to manage their health services from anywhere.</div></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Empower a Veteran-first approach</h3><div class="body"><p>The VA has been working to pave the way for a Veteran-focused digital experience, and this project was a landmark moment in propagating that approach throughout the organization. Human centered design and plain language are no longer the sole purview of digital experts — we developed systems that allow VA staff across the country to participate in the modernization of service delivery.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Improved customer experience</p><div class="body"><p>Veterans and caregivers can navigate the new VA medical center websites with ease. With 1 - 2 clicks, they can apply for benefits, schedule appointments, refill prescriptions, or learn more about VA services.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Secure data</p><div class="body"><p>The VA handles a lot of personally identifiable information, so we used an “API-first” approach that encapsulates data access behind an API that requires authentication.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Plain language</p><div class="body"><p>Service descriptions across VA websites were previously inconsistent and confusing. We helped analyze and restructure legacy content into user-friendly language, which was then applied across VA medical centers nationwide.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Informed product strategy</p><div class="body"><p>We worked with product designers responsible for the long-term digital modernization at VA, so they can better understand how to involve Drupal (their chosen CMS) in their product strategy.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Empowered content editors</p><div class="body"><p>Staff responsible for updating VA online content can do their jobs better with the new CMS. Smart governance processes powered by Drupal help content authors maintain consistency across VA-wide benefits information.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Increased usage of benefits</p><div class="body"><p>This work, as part of the large-scale modernization of VA.gov, has <a href="https://www.nextgov.com/it-modernization/2019/11/more-vets-are-taking-advantage-digital-services-through-new-vagov/161190/">resulted in more Veterans</a> interacting with VA services online. This means Veterans have more control and easier access to critical benefits and healthcare.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--staff"><div class="inner"><h2>Meet the class="inner"><h1>CivicActions announces 13 DITAP graduates across seven federal agencies</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Wednesday, September 8, 2021</p>
<p>CivicActions is pleased to announce the graduation of its newest <a href="https://civicactions.com/services/ditap">Digital IT Acquisition Professional (DITAP)</a> cohort, which included 13 procurement officers from seven federal agencies.</p>
<p>DITAP was created to modernize how the federal government buys digital services. Specifically, it teaches students how to build flexible contracts that keep pace with changing technologies.</p>
<p>“The coursework has been dynamic and relevant. It will empower us as acquisition professionals to be agile ambassadors and digital diplomats,” said DITAP graduate Rodney-Daryl Jones, who serves as the Director of Information Technology Acquisition for the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).</p>
<p>He shared his commentary during the DITAP graduation ceremony on Aug. 30, adding that he hoped his fellow graduates would see themselves as change agents for better government.</p>
<p>“We’re now a national resource to help modernize and protect the United States government so that our nation can thrive,” he said.</p>
<p>The six-month DITAP program starts by covering 21st century digital services — including agile software development, human-centered design, cloud computing and data management. Students then learn how to contract these services, and ensure their projects are successful.</p>
<p>DITAP also enables contracting officers to be business advisors and change agents within their own agencies. This serves DITAP’s bigger goal of building a culture of innovative acquisition across the federal government.</p>
<p>Upon DITAP graduation, students earn their Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting Core-Plus Specialization in Digital Services (<a href="https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/fac_c_digital_services_05_12_18.pdf?utm_medium=email&utm_source=govdelivery">FAC-C-DS</a>). By 2022, the FAC-C-DS will be required for all federal contracting officers who manage contracts of $7M or more.</p>
<p>With this cohort, CivicActions is pleased to congratulate the following DITAP graduates, which are listed by their agency:</p>
<h2>Department of Transportation (DOT)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Kyle Griggs, Contract Specialist</li>
</ul>
<h2>Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Christopher Davis, Contracting Officer</li>
<li>Darren Gann, Contracting Officer</li>
<li>Rodney-Daryl Jones, Director, Information Technology Acquisition</li>
</ul>
<h2>Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Yolanda Cooper, Contracting Officer</li>
</ul>
<h2>Health and Human Services (HHS)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Jennifer Browning, Branch Chief</li>
</ul>
<h2>National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Katie Cooney, Division Director, IT Hardware and Maintenance</li>
</ul>
<h2>National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Yolanda Robinson-Freeman, Manager, Specialty Acquisition Branch</li>
<li>Ernesto Jayme, Contract Specialist</li>
</ul>
<h2>United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Matthew Carnes, Contracting Officer</li>
<li>Robert Cortez, Contracting Officer</li>
<li>Scott Beckstrand, Chief, Strategic Acquisitions Division</li>
<li>Stuart Christianson, Contract Specialist</li>
</ul>
<p>CivicActions is proud to be the nation’s only small business that is fully-authorized  to provide DITAP training. For more information about our DITAP program, visit <a href="https://civicactions.com/services/ditap">civicactions.com/services/ditap</a>. class="inner"><h1>Accessibility Accelerator</h1><span class="client-name">OpenACR (Accessibility Conformance Reporting)</span><p class="body">Modernizing the ACR (Accessibility Conformance Reporting) Process</p></div></section><section class="section--case-study--challenge-to-tools"><div class="inner"><div class="case-study-challenge-goal"><div class="challenge"><h2>The challenge</h2><div class="body"><p>To ensure products used by the government are <a href="https://www.section508.gov/manage/join-the-508-community/">accessible</a>, vendors must submit accessibility conformance reports (ACR) to demonstrate their products meet <a href="https://www.section508.gov/">Section 508</a> requirements. The most commonly used ACR follows the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT), a templated Word Document or PDF that software vendors fill in manually, and often is not an accurate representation of product accessibility.</p>
<p>The ACR process is inconsistently structured, not searchable, static, and with no version control. For this reason, providing more accessible services can be complex and disempowering for vendors and procurement officers. The General Services Administration (GSA), which manages and supports the basic functioning of federal agencies, was interested in finding ways to modernize the ACR process. After requesting a Market Research Request for Information (RFI), we responded with the concept for OpenACR, a tool that simplifies the process of finding, sharing, and maintaining accurate and actionable data about product accessibility. After GSA reviewed potential solutions, CivicActions was awarded the contract for our innovative approach.</p>
<p><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/procurement_9e440e5e4e/procurement_9e440e5e4e.jpg" alt="procurement.jpg"></p></div></div></div><div class="case-study--expertise-tools"><div class="expertise"><h3>Expertise</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Accessibility, Section 508/WCAG</li>
<li>VPAT/ACR reporting</li>
<li>Information Architecture</li>
<li>Prototype Development & Testing</li>
<li>Usability testing</li>
<li>User and Stakeholder Research</li>
<li>Automated Testing</li>
</ul></div></div><div class="tools"><h3>Tools and technologies</h3><div class="body"><ul>
<li>Node</li>
<li>YAML and JSON</li>
<li>JavaScript/TypeScript</li>
<li>Svelte</li>
<li>HTML and CSS</li>
<li>Handlebars</li>
<li>U.S. Web Design System (USWDS)</li>
<li>GitHub Actions and Pages</li>
</ul></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--approaches"><div class="inner"><div class="first-approach"><h2>Our Approach</h2><div class="body"><p>Our team, led by Senior Strategist and accessibility expert Mike Gifford, realized that the process of managing ACRs hadn’t kept up with the nature of modern software development. Leveraging the YAML machine-readable language, the team created a highly structured report format that can be easily exported to an accessible and readable HTML document.</p></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach--with-image"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>OpenACR, Open Source</h3><div class="body"><p>Our team was excited to do the development process in the open. OpenACR is open source, so other organizations and members of the open source community are free to generate input and build on OpenACR’s source code. Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) worldwide have contributed to the development of this new tool, and all are welcome to visit the <a href="https://github.com/GSA/openacr/issues">open issue queue</a> to add feedback.</p></div></div><div class="image--wrapper"><div><img src="https://storage.googleapis.com/ca-it-prod-home-5918-strapi/production/overview_openacr_4042e002ce/overview_openacr_4042e002ce.png" alt=""></div></div></div></div><div class="inner"><div class="approach"><div class="title-text--wrapper"><h3>Foundational Accessibility</h3><div class="body"><p>OpenACR sets a new standard for foundational accessibility.  By building a machine-readable ACR, OpenACR allows for developing a central directory of accessibility standards for software used by the government. This is a significant milestone in standardizing accessibility practices and simplifies the process of communicating product accessibility for vendors and government IT buyers.</p></div></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--outcomes"><h2>Key outcomes</h2><div class="inner"><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Radically Improving Accessibility </p><div class="body"><p>OpenACR can reshape how procurement officers worldwide choose software for their organizations’ needs. By selecting more accessible tools, more organizations can set a higher standard of accessibility.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Cost and Time Savings Consolidation Tool </p><div class="body"><p>OpenACR includes a collection of tools that supports editing and validating Accessibility Conformance Reports (ACRs). The tools will eventually allow procurement officers to find, search, and compare accessibility reports with higher accuracy while simplifying the process for IT vendors to create useful ACRs, resulting in saving time and money.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Standardized, Machine-Readable ACR </p><div class="body"><p>Our team designed OpenACR to help Accessibility Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) create machine-readable documents built with YAML. This can be easily exported to an accessible and readable HTML document. The YAML format can also be easily imported and modified.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Open Source</p><div class="body"><p>Open ACR is an open source project, so other organizations are free to extend and improve the project.</p></div></div><div class="key-outcome"><p class="label">Foundational Standards</p><div class="body"><p>OpenACR can produce ACRs for Section 508 compliance but supports Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0 and WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion. The final HTML version follows the standard VPAT format.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section--case-study--staff"><div class="inner"><h2>Meet the team</h2><div class="inner"><h1>CivicActions Partners with Aplastic Anemia & MDS International Foundation (AAMDSIF) for Drupal 10 Migration</h1><p class="body"></p></div></section><div class="single--press-releases--main"><div class="inner"><div class="body"><div class="body"><p>Date: Friday, January 5, 2024</p>
<p>CivicActions is proud to announce its collaboration with the <a href="https://www.aamds.org/">Aplastic Anemia & MDS International Foundation (AAMDSIF)</a> to facilitate their migration from Drupal 7 to Drupal 10.</p>
<p>AAMDSIF is a nonprofit organization at the forefront of providing support to individuals and families affected by aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), and related bone marrow failure diseases. AAMDSIF provides answers, support, and hope to thousands of patients and their families around the world.</p>
<p>As passionate advocates of bringing an empathetic approach to healthcare, CivicActions is excited to support AAMDSIF to make their critical health information more accessible to patients and families.</p>
<p>The transition to Drupal 10 represents a strategic move to upgrade AAMDSIF’s digital infrastructure and ensure seamless access to vital resources by leveraging CivicActions’ 20 years of corporate experience in Drupal, an open source content management system. Daniel Mundra, Associate Director of Drupal at CivicActions with 13 years of experience in Drupal, will be leading this effort.</p>
<p>CivicActions has deep ties to the Drupal community, with nearly 200 Drupal Contributions since 2022 and a team consisting of several Acquia-certified Drupal developers, a Drupal Core Accessibility Maintainer, and a Drupal Core Initiative Coordinator. Their Drupal impact has been used to improve Drupal Core and the U.S. Web Design System (USWDS 2.0) through frequent contributions to modules and themes. Recent Drupal projects include work for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and the National Science Foundation (NSF).</p>
<p>This technically precise project for AAMDSIF will require highly detailed cross-linking and references, ultimately resulting in users having improved search functionality for the most up-to-date information, while simplifying website management for editors—thus allowing for an improved delivery of critical health information.</p>
<p>"We are excited to work with AAMDSIF in guiding this web platform upgrade using our expertise in Drupal," said Owen Barton, Chief Technology Officer, CivicActions. "This partnership perfectly aligns with our impact criteria, wherein we proactively select projects that reflect our values. Everyone at CivicActions is passionate about making a positive difference in the world, and our team is committed to supporting AAMDSIF in the critical work they are doing.”</p></div></div></div></div><section class="primary-page-cta"><div class="inner"><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__text"><h2>Inspired by newsworthy work?</h2><span class="h3">See what we can do together.</span></div><div class="cta-column primary-page-cta__buttons"><a class="button button__primary  " href="/services/">EXPLORE SERVICES</a><a class="button button__secondary  " href="/contracting/">CONTRACTING INFO</a></div></div></section></div></main><footer id="footer--section" class="footer" tabindex="-1"><div class="inner grid-container"><div class="grid-container__item footer__branding "><a href="/"><img class="footer__branding--logo" src="/static/ca-extended-logo-997e4b38802a3d9df0b2c636bf1c1bd9.svg" alt="Civic Actions Logo"></a></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__about-text"><div><p>We're a professional services firm providing design, technology, consulting, and training services to government.</p><p>Want to help us make an impact?<br><a href="/careers/">Check out our open positions.</a></p></div></div><div class="grid-container__item footer__contact"><div class="footer__contact-text"><p>Our mailing address is:<br>3527 Mt.
